title: Blakey as credential; advice to ask, and The Four Agreements
summary: Blakey's name gave Jackson confidence; he cites Blakey's advice to ask for what you want and The Four Agreements on not taking things personally.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: More times than not it does. More times than not it does. But for me, again, no disrespect to Ron, no disrespect to Les McCann, no disrespect to Kenny Barron or Freddie Hubbard, but I started with Art Blakey. If I’m sitting with Art Blakey and he’s talking about Charlie Parker and Sarah Vaughan, Thelonious Monk, John Coltrane, Miles Davis, those were his friends, Bud Powell, so that gave me the confidence because that was an American Express card. When I told people I was with Art Blakey I’d be right in. So I did have a little bit more of a caveat but I think that gave me confidence. As Art Blakey said, no one can stop you but you. And he would always say things like, “Don’t be a chicken and scratch for it, be a man and ask for it.” So if you want something you’ve got to reach out for it. And even if Mr. Carter said no, it wouldn’t be personal. Again, one of the greatest books I’ve ever read in my life is called The Four Agreements and it’s four agreements. And the agreements are: always do your best, don’t take things personal, be

impeccable with your word, and don’t assume. And I found that not taking anything personal, although it seems like it’s a hard concept, nothing is personal. If you got up right now and said I hate the way this interview is going and I hate the way this is working out, we’re done, you’re out of here. That’s not my issue. That’s something that you felt, that I can’t go inside of your mind to figure out. So it’s not personal. It was your choice. So it’s a hard concept, and it’s taken me years to really wrap myself around things, everyone makes choices that, at the end of the day, are their own personal choices, that have nothing to do with anybody else. That’s just what I believe. And so we all make a choice about whether we want success, about whether we want this, and with this and that, and then that choice we make propels us to do the work that we’re going to do. So if I want to start playing in the New York Symphony tomorrow, obviously it’s going to be a lot of arduous work, but also I’ve got to meet the people in that area, and I might have to play in the Syracuse Symphony on my way to the New York Symphony or I may never get to the New York Symphony. But the point of it is we are trying to work toward that point and you set a goal for yourself. And I just feel at the end of the day we are all getting what we ask for.
